did_you_know.text: Did you know? Jehoahaz son of Jehu ruled over the kingdom of Israel in Samaria for seventeen years, beginning his reign in the twenty-third year of Joash king of Judah.
Did you know? Although Jehoahaz did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, he pleaded with Him because of the severe oppression by the king of Aram—and the LORD listened to him.
Did you know? In response to Jehoahaz’s prayer, the LORD gave Israel a “deliverer,” and Israel was freed from Aram and returned to live securely in its tents, as in earlier times.
Did you know? The deliverance was only partial: Israel did not abandon the sins of the house of Jeroboam, and the Asherah pole still stood in Samaria.
Did you know? Jehoahaz’s army had been greatly reduced by the wars with Aram: only fifty horsemen, ten chariots, and ten thousand infantry remained.
Did you know? Joash son of Jehoahaz ruled over Israel for sixteen years, beginning his reign in the thirty-seventh year of Joash king of Judah.
Did you know? When Elisha fell ill with his final illness, Joash king of Israel came to him and wept over him, saying, “My father, my father, the chariots and horsemen of Israel!”
Did you know? Shooting the arrow eastward symbolized “the arrow of deliverance from the LORD”—Israel’s victory over Aram at Aphek.
Did you know? Elisha commanded Joash to strike the ground with the arrows, but Joash struck it only three times. So Elisha became angry with him, because he should have struck it five or six times.
Did you know? Even after Elisha’s death, his name was associated with a miracle: a man who was thrown into his tomb and touched his bones came back to life and stood on his feet.
